## README.md
# Mesic Analysis Platform — sagebrush biome

Mesic ground (wet meadows, springs and riparian floodplains) across the 14-state sagebrush biome,
from the Mesic Analysis Platform produced by Working Lands for Wildlife and the University of
Montana Numerical Terradynamic Simulation Group, with BLM Montana/Dakotas, the Intermountain West
Joint Venture and NRCS.

Mesic ground is a small share of the sagebrush landscape but carries a disproportionate amount of
its summer forage, brood-rearing habitat and late-season green vegetation, and it is not resolved
by coarse land-cover or fuels products.

## Source & attribution

**Source**: https://rangeland.ntsg.umt.edu/data/mesic/ (the `README` at that root is the authority)
**Method paper**: Mueller, K.R., Morford, S.L., Maestas, J.D., Kimball, J.S., Olsen, A.C., Wood, D.J.A., & Naugle, D.E. (in review). *Beyond Uplands: Integrating Riparian Areas into Sagebrush Conservation Design for a More Resilient West.* bioRxiv https://doi.org/10.64898/2025.12.29.696625
**License**: MIT, © 2025 University of Montana — redistribution permitted with attribution
**Accessed**: 2026-09-17T17:05:34Z (rasters, HUC12); 2026-10-13T20:37:11Z (valley bottoms)

Upstream replaces these files in place and publishes no edition label or immutable archive. The
staged copies under `raw/`, with their recorded sizes and sha256 checksums in `raw/PROVENANCE.txt` and `raw/PROVENANCE-valley-bottoms.txt`,
are the citable artifact. The `2026-09` in each dataset id is our build label, recording when
upstream last replaced the files; it is **not** an upstream release number.

## Footprint

The sagebrush biome across 14 states (AZ, CA, CO, ID, MT, NE, NV, NM, ND, OR, SD, UT, WA, WY).
Nothing here is clipped to a single state, and **Alaska lies wholly outside coverage**. A national
statistic computed from these layers has a 14-state denominator, not a country-wide one.

## Datasets

**Base URL**: `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-mesic/`

| Dataset | What it answers | H3 |
|---|---|---|
| `mesic-persistence-unmasked-2026-09` | How persistently mesic is the mesic ground, with no land-cover masking | native 10, parents 9, 8, 0 |
| `mesic-persistence-masked-2026-09` | Same, after upstream land-cover masking | native 10, parents 9, 8, 0 |
| `mesic-presence-2026-09` | How *much* mesic ground is present (the only route to a defensible area) | native 8, parent 0 |
| `mesic-huc12-2026-09` | Valley-bottom and mesic metrics per HUC12 subwatershed | native 8, parent 0 |
| `mesic-valley-bottoms-2026-09` | Individual valley-bottom segments with persistence, floodplain, tree cover, slope and stream class | none (GeoParquet + PMTiles) |

### Which persistence raster to use

| product | masking | use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `unmasked` | none — every pixel mesic in ≥1 year, any land cover | **forested / IRA analysis**, irrigated land, alpine |
| `masked` | valley bottoms keep all productive pixels except development and open water; **uplands** drop pixels over 10% tree cover | reliable mesic mapping outside forested uplands |

NoData means different things in the two: in `unmasked` it is "never mesic"; in `masked` it is
"never mesic **or** removed by the mask". Note `masked` is not the retired `Herbaceous` product,
which removed every ≥10%-tree pixel everywhere.

### Units: 1–42 years, not 0–100 percent

`Persistence` is a **count of the 42 analysed years** (1984–2025, excluding 2012), not a percentage.
The upstream README contradicts itself; the data settles it. Published unscaled — divide by 42 for
a percent.

## ⛔ Do not compute mesic area by counting COG pixels

The rasters are EPSG:4326 with a pixel size in **degrees**, so a pixel covers ~900 × cos(latitude)
m², not 900 m². Counting valid pixels × 900 m² overstates mesic extent by ~37% across this
footprint.

| method | mesic area |
|---|---:|
| `mesic-presence-2026-09` hex, fraction × true H3 cell area | **987,608 km²** |
| naive COG pixel count × 900 m² | 1,356,638 km² |

Use the presence hex. H3 cells carry true spherical area; a geographic-CRS pixel does not.

## HUC12: 18,853 watersheds, and `huc12` is derived by us

The source GeoPackage holds **20,032 rows, of which 1,179 are exact duplicates** (identical geometry
*and* identical attributes). Those repeats are removed here. A total taken from the source file
directly is inflated by about 6%.

It also ships **no HUC code** — only an ambiguous `name`. The `huc12` column is **derived by us** by
matching each boundary to the USGS Watershed Boundary Dataset by geometric overlap, with an exact
name match used only to place a boundary that overlap alone could not. Every assigned code is
unique. Three watersheds read empty because their boundary spans several WBD watersheds and
matches none by name. This is what lets the table join to `usgs-wbd-hu12` on `huc12` and on `h8`.

## Valley bottoms: 23,062,045 segments, no hex

The source GeoPackage holds **24,690,182 rows, of which 1,628,137 repeat a segment already
present**, some up to 10 times. Those repeats are removed here. A total of `Area_m2` taken from the
source file directly is inflated by about 29%.

Most segments are smaller than one H3 resolution 10 cell, so this layer has no hex index. Use the
persistence and presence collections for cell-level work.

Two upstream columns need care, and are published unchanged:

- **`DstCore_Km`**: about 8.3 million segments read 1,000 to 1,262 km. Those values rise steadily
  from north to south across the whole biome, so they do not measure distance to core. Filter
  `DstCore_Km < 1000`.
- **`FldPln_Pct`**: not capped at 100. About 2.5 million segments read above 100, almost all 101
  to 110. Cap it with `LEAST(FldPln_Pct, 100)` before averaging.

## Access

### DuckDB

```sql
INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial; INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;

-- Mesic area of a region, from the presence layer
SELECT SUM(mesic_fraction * h3_cell_area(h8, 'km^2')) AS mesic_km2
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-mesic/mesic-presence-2026-09/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet');

-- Watershed metrics: reduce to one row per watershed BEFORE totalling
SELECT SUM(area_vb_m2) / 1e6 AS valley_bottom_km2 FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT _cng_fid, area_vb_m2
  FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-mesic/mesic-huc12-2026-09/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet')
);

-- Join persistence to the watershed table on h8
SELECT w.huc12, AVG(p.persistence) AS mean_years
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-mesic/mesic-huc12-2026-09/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet') w
JOIN read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-mesic/mesic-persistence-unmasked-2026-09/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet') p
  USING (h8)
GROUP BY w.huc12;
```

The flat GeoParquet is at `mesic-huc12-2026-09.parquet`.

```sql
-- Valley-bottom area by stream class, with a capped, area-weighted floodplain share
SELECT Strm_Type,
       SUM(Area_m2) / 1e6 AS valley_bottom_km2,
       SUM(LEAST(FldPln_Pct, 100) * Area_m2) / SUM(Area_m2) AS floodplain_pct
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-mesic/mesic-valley-bottoms-2026-09.parquet')
GROUP BY Strm_Type;
```

### MapLibre GL JS

The PMTiles **`source-layer` is `mesic-huc12-2026-09`**.

```js
map.addSource('mesic-huc12', {
  type: 'vector',
  url: 'pmtiles://https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-mesic/mesic-huc12-2026-09.pmtiles'
});

map.addLayer({
  id: 'mesic-huc12-fill',
  type: 'fill',
  source: 'mesic-huc12',
  'source-layer': 'mesic-huc12-2026-09',
  paint: {
    'fill-color': [
      'interpolate', ['linear'], ['get', 'prHuc_vb'],
      0, '#F5F0E6', 0.1, '#A6BDDB', 0.3, '#2C7FB8', 0.6, '#253494'
    ],
    'fill-opacity': 0.8
  }
});
```

`mgmt_code`: 0 = Other/None, 1 = Protect & Maintain, 2 = Restore & Enhance, 3 = Strategic Management.

The valley-bottom PMTiles **`source-layer` is `mesic-valley-bottoms-2026-09`**.

```js
map.addSource('mesic-valley-bottoms', {
  type: 'vector',
  url: 'pmtiles://https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-mesic/mesic-valley-bottoms-2026-09.pmtiles'
});

map.addLayer({
  id: 'mesic-valley-bottoms-fill',
  type: 'fill',
  source: 'mesic-valley-bottoms',
  'source-layer': 'mesic-valley-bottoms-2026-09',
  paint: {
    'fill-color': [
      'interpolate', ['linear'], ['get', 'Veg_Pct'],
      0, '#F5F0E6', 25, '#A1D99B', 50, '#41AB5D', 100, '#005A32'
    ],
    'fill-opacity': 0.8
  }
});
```

### Rasters

The three COGs are at `mesic-persistence-unmasked-2026-09-cog.tif`,
`mesic-persistence-masked-2026-09-cog.tif` and `mesic-presence-2026-09-cog.tif`, all EPSG:4326,
30 m, and readable by titiler or any GDAL client.

## Caveats

- **Never SUM on the hex.** Persistence is a per-pixel average year count; on the HUC12 hex every
  attribute is a per-watershed value repeated on each covered cell. Reduce to one row per watershed
  on `huc12` (or `_cng_fid`) first.
- **`mean` persistence is not mesic area.** A cell holding one 42-year pixel and a cell holding 500
  both read 42. Use `mesic-presence-2026-09` for area.
- **Presence is a full grid** — a `0` is "no mesic pixels", not "no data". Clip to the biome
  footprint before computing totals.
- **Upstream filtering on the vector product:** valley-bottom segments over 25% persistent open
  water or with mean bare ground ≥85% are excluded, so "valley bottom area" is not all valley
  bottom.
- `prV_Pub` / `prV_Prv` derive from **PAD-US 2025** — check against `pad-us-4.1` rather than
  assuming agreement.

Full STAC metadata: `stac-collection.json` at the bucket root and under each dataset prefix.
